summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR326.7 crore, but gross margin fell to 34.1% and PAT to INR13.5 crore (4.1% margin).
summary.overview: Revenue grew 28% YoY on domestic growth of 60%, while exports were flat at about 1.3%. Gross margin compressed about 540 bps to 34.1% from raw material inflation and new-product learning-curve effects. EBITDA rose 12.6% to INR29.6 crore at a 9% margin. H1 PAT fell 9.3% to INR35.5 crore because about INR9 crore of prior-year other income (FX gains and tax-refund interest) did not recur. Management said deferred export orders should flow into Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.value: 19% of revenue (about INR62 crore per analyst)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR7.7 crore in H1 FY26; entirely working capital

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue up 60% YoY in Q2, driven mainly by new products supplied as advanced intermediates to Indian customers who convert them to technicals or formulations for export. Existing products also grew.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue up only about 1.3% YoY in Q2; H1 export growth was 13.6%. Management attributed the slowdown to customer orders deferred from Q1/Q2 into Q3/Q4, especially Europe, where unusually hot weather delayed sowing.

segments.name: Segment reporting
segments.commentary: Company follows single-segment accounting under Performance Chemicals, so no segment-wise revenue split was given despite the Agrochemicals, Specialty, Pharma and Industrial Chemicals portfolio description.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be good quarters and that the previously guided targets should be achievable.
Deferred volumes from Q1 and Q2 are expected to be serviced in H2 FY27; the amount was not quantified.
MoU products expected to contribute INR15-20 crore in FY28, with gradual ramp-up over the next two years toward INR30-50 crore per product per year.
Trade receivables, which rose to above INR450 crore at 30 September 2026 from INR203.5 crore in FY26, are expected to fall in Q3 and Q4 and return to normal range by year-end.
Gross margin expected to recover to normal levels as the company moves down the learning curve on new products.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation above 80% across Derabassi, Lalru and Pune plants in Q1 and Q2; some sites can exceed 90%.
New manufacturing block at Lalru to add agrochemical and intermediate capacity for incremental business and pipeline products.
Planned capex of about INR100 crore for a new project, funded 25% equity (internal accruals) and 75% debt, with additional debt sanction already in place.
Greenfield site shortlisting is at an advanced stage; no location finalised yet, and the company will inform exchanges once it is.
H1 FY27 capex about INR28 crore, of which incremental gross block was about INR16 crore; the rest was capital advances. Management said the spend is asset renewal, as assets are about 40 years old.
demand_pricing: Indian agrochemical demand was weak in H1 FY27 due to weak monsoon, delayed sowing, uneven rains and geopolitical supply disruptions.
Solvent prices rose about 10-40% and other raw materials 5-15%; yield gains absorbed part of the increase.
New products were priced competitively while raw material costs rose, compressing margins on those products.
Credit terms were extended to major international customers due to geopolitical conditions, which lifted receivables.
R&D spend is about 2% of revenue; the company added a PhD scientist and three postgraduates and is revamping its pilot plant for scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: How much shipment was deferred, and why did revenue fall about INR20 crore sequentially despite 80%+ utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sequential comparisons are distorted by product mix; Q1 utilisation was 3-4 points higher than Q2. It declined to quantify the deferred amount, saying the volume will be serviced in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall despite higher new-product share (19% in Q2)?
qa_highlights.answer: Two factors: learning-curve inefficiency during scale-up, and raw material prices rising faster than product prices, compressing new-product margins. Management expects volume growth and cost competitiveness to restore margins over time.

qa_highlights.question: Capex of about INR28 crore in H1 but only about INR16 crore incremental gross block; what is the INR12 crore difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spend is asset renewal on assets about 40 years old, and that a greenfield project is at an advanced stage with shortlisted plots.

qa_highlights.question: Funding mix and debt needs for the INR100 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding is about 25% equity and 75% debt. Equity will come from internal accruals, and additional debt sanction is already in place, to be drawn as the project progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables jump from INR203.5 crore in FY26 to over INR450 crore at September 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Extended credit terms were granted to major international customers because of geopolitical conditions. Management expects receivables to fall in Q3 and Q4 and reach a normal range by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue can the MoU products contribute in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Each product was guided at INR30-50 crore a year. Due to long overseas approval cycles (Japan, Europe), FY28 is expected to be INR15-20 crore, with gradual ramp-up over two years.

risks_watch: Gross margin at 34.1% versus 39.5% a year ago; recovery depends on new-product learning curve and raw material pricing.
Receivables above INR450 crore; collection in Q3 and Q4 needs to be verified.
Deferred export demand must convert into Q3/Q4 shipments, especially Europe and Japan.
Rising debt to fund about INR100 crore capex, with finance cost already up 27% in H1.
Non-recurrence of about INR9 crore other income in H1 keeps PAT under pressure.
Greenfield site and MoU product approvals remain pending, with long overseas qualification cycles.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and new-product pipeline, but cautious and vague on near-term numbers. Management declined to quantify deferred shipments and segment revenue, and deflected sequential comparisons to product mix. Its expectation of a strong H2 rests on unquantified order deferrals.
